blogPosts.title: How Much Does Lawn Mowing Cost in Torquay?
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the real cost of professional lawn mowing in Torquay in 2026. We break down pricing factors, frequency options, and what to expect from a quality local service.
body: If you are a Torquay homeowner wondering how much lawn mowing costs in 2026, you are not alone. With rising fuel costs and increased demand for lawn care services across the Surf Coast, understanding pricing helps you budget wisely. On average, professional lawn mowing in Torquay ranges from $50 to $90 for a standard residential block, depending on the size of your lawn, the frequency of service, and any additional requirements such as edging, line trimming, or green waste removal. At Torquay Lawn Masters, we pride ourselves on transparent, upfront pricing so there are never any surprises when the job is done.

Several factors influence the cost of lawn mowing in Torquay. The most significant is the overall size of your lawn, measured in square metres. A compact front yard on a standard Torquay residential block will naturally cost less than a large rear lawn that backs onto open space. Terrain also plays a role. Lawns with steep slopes, uneven ground, or obstacles like garden beds, retaining walls, and swimming pools require more time and specialised equipment. Additionally, the condition of your lawn matters. An overgrown yard that has not been mowed in weeks will take longer and may incur a higher initial fee compared to a well-maintained lawn on a regular care schedule.

Frequency is another key factor in determining your lawn mowing costs in Torquay. Most homeowners opt for weekly or fortnightly service, which typically offers better per-visit pricing than one-off mows. Weekly mowing keeps your lawn at an optimal height, promoting thicker growth and reducing the time needed per visit. Fortnightly service works well during cooler months when grass growth slows down, particularly during Torquay's mild winters. Many Torquay Lawn Masters clients save money by signing up for a regular maintenance plan, which locks in a consistent rate and ensures their lawn never gets ahead of them. We offer flexible scheduling to suit every lifestyle and budget.

Location within Torquay can also affect pricing. Properties closer to the beach or in areas like Jan Juc may experience faster grass growth during spring and summer due to higher moisture levels and milder temperatures. This can mean more frequent mowing is required to keep your lawn looking its best. Our team at Torquay Lawn Masters services the entire Torquay area from our Marine Drive base, and we factor in local conditions when recommending a mowing schedule. We also consider grass type, as different varieties such as Couch, Kikuyu, and Buffalo grass have different growth rates and mowing requirements, which can influence both frequency and cost.

When comparing lawn mowing prices in Torquay, it is important to look beyond the headline rate and consider what is included. Some operators charge extra for edging, line trimming, and blowing down hard surfaces. At Torquay Lawn Masters, our standard mowing service includes all of these essentials. We arrive with professional-grade equipment, complete the job efficiently, and leave your property looking immaculate. We also take away all grass clippings and green waste, so you do not have to worry about bagging and disposal. Our all-inclusive approach means the price we quote is the price you pay, with no hidden extras.

If you are looking for affordable, reliable lawn mowing in Torquay, we recommend getting a free on-site quote from a local provider like Torquay Lawn Masters. A quick visit allows us to assess your lawn size, condition, and access requirements, ensuring we provide an accurate and fair price. We never lock you into long-term contracts, so you can try our service with complete confidence. Whether you need a one-off tidy-up before a Torquay real estate inspection or regular weekly care for your family home, we are here to help. Contact us today to arrange your free Torquay lawn mowing quote.

blogPosts.title: Best Grass Types for Torquay and the Surf Coast
blogPosts.excerpt: Choosing the right grass for your Torquay lawn matters. We compare Buffalo, Kikuyu, and Couch varieties suited to the Surf Coast climate and sandy coastal soils.
body: Choosing the right grass type for your Torquay lawn is one of the most important decisions you can make as a homeowner. The Surf Coast's unique climate, characterised by mild winters, warm summers, salty coastal breezes, and predominantly sandy soils, significantly impacts which grass varieties will thrive. Selecting a grass that is poorly suited to Torquay's conditions can lead to a patchy, struggling lawn that requires constant intervention. This guide covers the best grass types for Torquay and the broader Surf Coast region, helping you make an informed choice for a lawn that stays green, healthy, and low-maintenance throughout the year.

Buffalo grass is arguably the most popular choice for Torquay lawns, and for good reason. Modern Buffalo varieties like Sir Walter, Sapphire, and Palmetto are exceptionally well-suited to coastal conditions. They tolerate salt spray, handle partial shade, and maintain a deep green colour with relatively low water requirements. Buffalo's broad leaf blades create a thick, lush carpet that resists weed invasion and stands up well to family foot traffic. For Torquay homeowners with established trees or gardens that receive mixed sun and shade throughout the day, Buffalo grass offers the versatility and resilience needed to look great in all conditions across the seasons.

Kikuyu grass is another excellent option for Torquay properties with full sun exposure. This vigorous, fast-growing grass is ideal for larger lawns, play areas, and properties where a robust, durable surface is needed. Kikuyu handles Torquay's summer heat well and recovers quickly from wear and tear, making it perfect for families with children or pets. However, its aggressive growth habit means it requires regular mowing and edging to prevent it from invading garden beds and pathways. In Torquay's coastal climate, Kikuyu establishes quickly and provides excellent ground cover, but it is best suited to open, sunny areas where its vigorous nature is an advantage rather than a challenge.

Couch grass, particularly Santa Ana and other hybrid varieties, is well-suited to the drier, sunnier spots in Torquay gardens. Couch forms a dense, fine-textured lawn that tolerates heavy foot traffic and recovers well from damage. It thrives in full sun and handles Torquay's warm summers with ease, going dormant and turning brown during the cooler winter months before greening up again in spring. For Torquay homeowners who want a pristine, bowling-green appearance, Couch grass delivers a manicured look that is hard to beat. It does require more frequent mowing during peak growing season and benefits from regular fertilisation to maintain its dense, vibrant appearance throughout the Surf Coast summer.

When selecting grass for your Torquay lawn, soil preparation is just as important as the grass variety itself. Torquay's sandy coastal soils drain quickly and often lack the organic matter needed for robust grass growth. Before laying any turf, we recommend a thorough soil test and amendment process. Adding quality topsoil, organic matter, and the right fertiliser blend creates a nutrient-rich foundation that helps your chosen grass establish faster and grow stronger. At Torquay Lawn Masters, we always prepare the soil properly before laying new turf, because we know that even the best grass variety will underperform without a solid foundation beneath it.

Timing is also critical when installing new lawn in Torquay. The best time to lay turf on the Surf Coast is during spring or early autumn, when temperatures are mild and rainfall is more consistent. This gives your new lawn the best chance to establish its root system before the stress of summer heat or winter dormancy. If you are considering a new lawn for your Torquay property, we recommend consulting with a local lawn care professional who understands the specific conditions in your area. The team at Torquay Lawn Masters can assess your site, recommend the ideal grass variety, and handle the full installation process from soil preparation through to first mow.

blogPosts.title: How to Restore a Damaged Lawn in Torquay
blogPosts.excerpt: Is your Torquay lawn looking damaged or patchy? Learn how to diagnose the cause and restore your lawn to a healthy, green state with expert local advice.
body: A damaged lawn is one of the most common issues Torquay homeowners face, whether caused by harsh summer weather, pet damage, heavy foot traffic, or simply neglect over the cooler months. The good news is that most lawn damage can be repaired without the need for a complete re-turf. Understanding the cause of the damage and applying the right restoration technique is key to getting your Torquay lawn back to its green, healthy best. In this guide, we walk you through the step-by-step process of assessing, treating, and restoring damaged lawn areas right here on the Surf Coast.

The first step in any lawn restoration is identifying what caused the damage in the first place. In Torquay, the most common causes include drought stress during hot summers, fungal diseases in the damp winter months, soil compaction from heavy traffic, pet urine burn patches, and scalping from mowing too low. Each cause requires a different approach. For example, drought-damaged lawns need deep, infrequent watering and a wetting agent to help sandy Torquay soils absorb moisture. Fungal issues require improved drainage and potentially a fungicide treatment. Pet damage and scalping can usually be repaired with targeted reseeding or turf patching combined with improved lawn care practices.

For small damaged areas, overseeding or patching with fresh turf is the most effective restoration method. Start by removing any dead or dying grass and loosening the top 20 to 30 millimetres of soil. Apply a quality lawn starter fertiliser and either broadcast seed over the area or lay small turf patches, ensuring good soil-to-seed or soil-to-turf contact. Keep the area consistently moist for the first two to three weeks while the new growth establishes. In Torquay's sandy soils, this may mean watering lightly once or twice daily during warm weather. A layer of quality lawn topdressing over seeded areas helps retain moisture and protects new seedlings from wind and birds.

For larger areas of damage or lawns that have deteriorated significantly, a more comprehensive restoration may be needed. This typically involves scarifying or dethatching the entire lawn to remove dead material and thatch build-up, followed by aeration to relieve soil compaction. Core aeration is particularly important in Torquay where sandy soils can become compacted in high-traffic areas. After aeration, apply a layer of quality topdressing mix, ideally a blend of sand, organic matter, and soil that suits Torquay's coastal conditions. This process improves soil structure, enhances nutrient uptake, and creates the ideal environment for your lawn to recover and thicken up over the following weeks.

Ongoing lawn care after restoration is critical to preventing the damage from returning. Establishing a regular mowing schedule at the correct height for your grass type, fertilising seasonally, and watering appropriately are the three pillars of a healthy Torquay lawn. During summer, water deeply but infrequently to encourage deep root growth, which makes your lawn more drought-tolerant. In winter, reduce watering and raise your mowing height slightly to protect the grass from cold and disease. A regular fertilisation program, timed to the Surf Coast's growing seasons, provides the nutrients your lawn needs to stay thick, green, and resistant to weeds and pest damage.

If your Torquay lawn is looking worse for wear and you are not sure where to start, the team at Torquay Lawn Masters can help. We offer professional lawn assessment and restoration services tailored to the specific conditions of your property. From identifying the cause of the damage to implementing a full recovery plan, we handle every step of the process. Our local knowledge of Torquay's soil types, climate patterns, and grass varieties means we can recommend the most effective and cost-efficient restoration approach for your situation. Contact us for a free on-site assessment and let us bring your Torquay lawn back to life.

blogPosts.title: Summer Lawn Care Tips for Torquay Homeowners
blogPosts.excerpt: Keep your Torquay lawn green and healthy through summer with expert tips on watering, mowing height, fertilising, and pest prevention for Surf Coast conditions.
body: Summer on the Surf Coast is a wonderful time to enjoy your outdoor space, but the combination of high temperatures, increased UV exposure, and Torquay's sandy coastal soils can put serious stress on your lawn. Without the right care routine, even a healthy lawn can quickly turn brown and patchy during a Torquay summer. The key to keeping your grass green and vibrant through the warmer months is a proactive approach that addresses watering, mowing, fertilising, and pest prevention. In this guide, we share our top summer lawn care tips specifically tailored for Torquay homeowners looking to keep their lawns in peak condition.

Watering is the single most important factor in summer lawn care for Torquay properties. The sandy soils that are common throughout the Surf Coast drain water quickly, meaning your lawn needs less frequent but deeper watering to encourage deep root growth. We recommend watering your Torquay lawn early in the morning, ideally before 7 am, to reduce evaporation and give the grass time to absorb moisture before the heat of the day. Aim for one to two deep soaking sessions per week rather than light daily sprinkles. This approach trains roots to grow deeper into the soil profile, making your lawn significantly more drought-tolerant and resilient during Torquay's hottest summer days.

Mowing height is critical during summer and is one of the most common mistakes Torquay homeowners make. It is tempting to cut the grass short for a neat, manicured appearance, but scalping your lawn during summer removes the leaf canopy that shades the soil and protects the crown of the grass plant. This leads to rapid moisture loss, increased weed germination, and heat stress. During Torquay's summer months, raise your mowing height by 10 to 20 millimetres above your grass type's recommended height. For Buffalo grass, aim for around 50 to 60 millimetres. For Couch and Kikuyu, keep it at 30 to 40 millimetres. Always use sharp mower blades to ensure clean cuts that heal quickly.

Fertilising your Torquay lawn in summer should be approached with care. While regular feeding is important, applying too much nitrogen during hot weather can actually burn your grass and increase water demand. We recommend using a slow-release, summer-safe fertiliser blend that provides steady nutrition without the risk of scorching. A light application in early summer, followed by a second application in late summer, keeps your lawn well-fed without overwhelming it. Adding a wetting agent to your fertiliser program is also highly beneficial in Torquay's sandy soils, as it helps water penetrate the soil more evenly and reach the root zone where it is needed most.

Summer also brings increased pest pressure to Torquay lawns. African black beetle grubs, army worm, and billbugs are among the most common lawn pests that cause damage during the warmer months. Signs of pest damage include brown patches that do not respond to watering, spongy areas underfoot, and visible insects on the lawn surface in the early morning or evening. Prevention is always better than cure, so regular lawn inspections during summer are essential. If you notice unusual patching or deterioration in your Torquay lawn, a professional pest assessment can identify the issue early and prevent it from spreading across your entire lawn.

Weed control is another essential component of summer lawn maintenance in Torquay. Warm, moist conditions combined with regular watering create ideal circumstances for weed germination. Common summer weeds in Torquay include clover, bindii, oxalis, and various broadleaf species that can quickly invade thin or stressed areas of your lawn. A thick, healthy lawn is the best defence against weeds, so maintaining proper mowing height, adequate nutrition, and consistent watering naturally suppresses weed growth. For persistent weed problems, a targeted herbicide application may be necessary. The Torquay Lawn Masters team can assess your lawn and recommend the most effective weed management strategy for your specific grass type and garden conditions.
